title: C525 — Front door latch release motor LH
introduction:
This reference maps the left-hand front door latch release motor’s connector. I read its functions as separate conversations: lock commands tell the mechanism what to do, while latch-switch signals report information. Sharing a connector does not make those messages interchangeable—an address book still needs the right name beside each address.

Begin with the identification table, locate a cavity label in the drawing, then read its matching table row across for the circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal information. Shaded positions align with rows whose circuit and function fields are blank. The repeated ground/trim-switch cavity entry and the disagreement between the metadata count and the illustrated layout remain unresolved.

The pigtail sections provide service identifiers, including a separate European listing. This is a reference-reading guide: physical viewing direction, gauge convention and catalog-code meanings are unspecified. Access, probing, testing, wire selection and replacement need separate instructions.

edits.why: The elongated rounded housing has cavity labels running vertically and housing projections along the left edge. Shaded and outlined positions help connect the illustration with blank and populated circuit rows respectively. I use those details to navigate this drawing, without assigning a release function to the projections. The illustration does not identify its physical viewing side, so it cannot establish probing orientation.

The Function column distinguishes driver latch ajar and unlock switch entries, ground, the driver trim door-lock switch connection, all-lock control and driver-unlock control. Read Circuit Number alongside Function rather than treating every connection as a motor feed. The repeated cavity label carries both ground and trim-switch entries without a configuration qualifier; this does not establish a shared connection or identify which entry applies. Blank circuit rows are not instructions to add wiring.

Match Kit List to Number and Hard Shell to Engineering Shell to connect the connector record with its service listing. Service Part is the service identifier, while Image is an image filename. The kit’s Gauge and Material fields describe that listing; they do not replace the individual circuit entries or establish a wire-substitution or installation method.

The separate Product Id field provides the European pigtail identifier. I keep that regional listing distinct from the preceding Service Part field; its presence alone does not establish regional vehicle applicability, interchangeability or installation instructions.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count conflicts with the cavity count shown by both the illustration and the pigtail Cavities entry. The supplied evidence does not reconcile them.

A repeated cavity label carries differing ground and driver trim-switch circuit entries, with blank Qualifier fields. The evidence does not establish their configuration applicability or whether they describe a shared connection.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 41 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 4 edits. Count and repeated ground/trim-switch relationship ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
